shared_elements: quadruped animal shown in strict profile with visible legs
low-relief carving on a flat dressed stone face
bird-like or beaked creature in profile
stacked/superimposed animal motifs (one figure above another)
pillar edge or vertical framing arris of the block
surrounding rubble stonework at the base
justification: Both show shallow, rounded low relief of a profile quadruped with bent, articulated legs and a curled tail carved directly on the flat face of an upright stone block, with smaller animal forms placed below the main beast. The biggest difference is density and organisation: A is a crowded multi-register composition with a horizontal patterned band, disc, and many stacked creatures, whereas B is dominated by a single large isolated animal with only a faint motif beneath, and the two surfaces differ markedly in colour and finish.
